html:
A war between Chalcis and Eretria, the two leading cities of the island of Euboea, over the fertile Lelantine plain between them. It is usually dated to the late 8th or early 7th century BCE.

The two cities had been partners in trade and in early colonisation, founding settlements in Italy and the north Aegean. Thucydides says that in this war the rest of Greece split into alliances, more than in any other war before the Persian invasions. Later sources put Samos and Corinth on the side of Chalcis, and Miletus on the side of Eretria, though this is uncertain.

Little else is known. Chalcis seems to have won, and Eretria declined for a time. Hesiod tells of winning a poetry prize at funeral games in Chalcis for a nobleman later said to have fallen in the fighting. Because it set many Greek cities against each other, it is often seen as a first sign of the alliance wars that led much later to the Peloponnesian War.
